english.title: Attempt to breach a restraining order after conviction
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) without reasonable excuse, you attempted to **(..SPECIFY CONDUCT..) which you were prohibited from doing by a restraining order under section 5 of the protection from Harassment Act 1997 imposed by

(A)_[**(..SPECIFY..) Magistrates' Court]_
(B)_[**(..SPECIFY..) Crown Court]_

on **(..SPECIFY DATE OF ISSUE OF RESTRAINING ORDER..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 5(5) and (6) of the Protection from Harassment Act 1997 andsection 1(1) of the Criminal Attempts Act 1981.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Note – this offence applies to breaches of orders made under section 5 of the Protection from Harassment Act 1997, the breaches occurring on or before the 30th November 2020. Section 5 was repealed by the Sentencing Act 2020 on the 1st December 2020. Breaches of a section 5 order, which occur, on or after 1st December 2020, should be prosecuted under section 360 of the Sentencing Act 2020 H22093.
(iii) Unlike section 2 and section 4, one act is sufficient to breach the restraining order.

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Five years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
